title: ci: registry-free GPU job (runner-local SIF) + verify the provisioned overlay from a fresh session
body:
Two CI infra fixes that interact, in one PR.

## Registry-free GPU job

The job logged in to Docker Hub on every run to pull a private image. With the credentials rotated, the
unconditional login step fails before any test runs, although the SIF is cached and the pull is skipped.
The image is just Ubuntu + Python + torch; `run_fa4_ci.py` installs cutlass-dsl / quack / FA4 at job time.

- `gpu-test`: new input `fa4_local_sif` — use that SIF, skip pull and prune, fail if the file is missing.
- `ci.yml`: Docker Hub login only when `vars.FA4_LOCAL_SIF` is empty. Unset = unchanged behaviour.
- `tools/ci/docker/build_local_sif.sh`: `docker build` the existing Dockerfile on the runner and
  `apptainer build` a SIF into `CI_WORK_DIR/local-sif/` (registry mode prunes `*.sif` directly under
  `CI_WORK_DIR`, hence the subdirectory).

## Verify the provisioned overlay from a fresh session

All 8 tests failed with `JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ CuteDSLRT_TVMFFISetRaisedCudaError ]`
after a passing floor check. The test session saw the SIF-baked cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 runtime (`lib/`) next to
the installed 4.8.0 (`cu13/lib/`): `apptainer exec` returns before its fuse2fs child has flushed the overlay
image, so the next session can read a stale view, and DSL discovery tries `lib/` first. Intermittent and
load-dependent; latent since #2685, fatal once #2798 moved the pin off the SIF's layout. The floor check
runs in the same session as the install, so it cannot see this.

`tools/ci/run_fa4_ci.py`: wait until nothing holds the overlay image between sessions; verify from a fresh
session (one distribution per package, `flash_attn.cute` from the checkout, runtime owned by the installed
cutlass-dsl), re-provision once, then fail with `OVERLAY VERIFY FAILED: ...`; pin the verified runtime via
`CUTE_DSL_LIBS`.

## Validation

- Action pull step run locally in all three states (local SIF selected / missing file → exit 1 / variable
  unset → old cached-SIF path).
- Verification fails on an `--overlay img:ro` mount (whiteouts ignored, i.e. the leaked state), passes on RW.
- End-to-end with the `ci.yml` filter on the current CI SIF (DSL 4.6.0 baked) and on a
  `build_local_sif.sh` image (4.8.0 baked): verify OK, Pass 1 8/8, Pass 2 8/8 on both.

Related: #2685, #2798. Supersedes #2895.

title: ci: verify the provisioned overlay from a fresh session and pin the DSL runtime
body:
## Problem

Every GPU job on `main` failed on 2026-09-16, all 8 tests at `cute.compile(..., "--enable-tvm-ffi")`:

```
JIT session error: Symbols not found: [ CuteDSLRT_TVMFFISetRaisedCudaError ]
```

right after provisioning had reported `DSL floor check OK: nvidia-cutlass-dsl=4.8.0.dev0`.

Inside the failing test container the SIF-baked cutlass-dsl 4.6.0 runtime (`nvidia_cutlass_dsl/lib/`) was
visible next to the freshly installed 4.8.0 (`cu13/lib/`), although `prepare_overlay()` had deleted it and the
overlay image's upper layer on disk had the correct whiteouts and opaque marker. `apptainer exec` returns
before the fuse2fs that owns the ext3 image has finished flushing, so a session opened right after can read a
stale view. DSL runtime discovery tries `lib/` before `cu{major}/lib/`, so the stale 4.6.0 runtime was linked.
Intermittent and load-dependent. Latent since #2685; fatal once #2798 moved the pin from `==4.6.0.dev0`
(same layout as the SIF) to `>=4.6.2` (new `cu13/` layout).

The floor check runs in the same session as the install, where the in-memory overlay state is always right,
so it cannot see a cross-session inconsistency.

## Change (`tools/ci/run_fa4_ci.py`)

1. `wait_for_overlay_release()`: after every session, wait until no process holds the overlay image
   (60 s cap, then warn). `sync` at the end of provisioning.
2. `verify_overlay()`: a fresh session asserts one visible distribution per runtime package, `flash_attn.cute`
   imported from the checkout, and the `libcute_dsl_runtime` resolved by `get_shared_libs()` owned by the
   installed cutlass-dsl. On failure: recreate + re-provision once, then fail with `OVERLAY VERIFY FAILED: ...`
   naming what leaked, instead of 8 opaque JIT link errors.
3. Pin the verified runtime into the test sessions via `CUTE_DSL_LIBS`.

`tools/ci/README.md` documents the step.

## Validation

- The verification snippet fails on an `--overlay img:ro` mount (read-only mounts ignore whiteouts, i.e. the

title: ci: add PyTorch 2.14 to the wheel build matrix
body:
## Why

PyTorch 2.14 raised the `ATen/ATen.h` header guard to C++20 (pytorch/pytorch#178150), and FA2's `setup.py` hardcodes `-std=c++17`, so building against 2.14 fails with `#error C++20 or later compatible compiler is required to use ATen` (#2863). Nothing in CI compiles FA2 against any torch newer than 2.10, so the break was only found by users building from source.

Adding 2.14 to the wheel matrix does two things:

1. Moves the failure from the user's `pip install` into the release build: the next time a torch release changes a header requirement, a `v*` tag build fails instead of a user's source build.
2. Gives 2.14 users a prebuilt wheel. `setup.py` derives the wheel name from `torch.__version__` and `torch.version.cuda` and downloads it from the release; today 2.14 users miss (no such asset), fall back to a source build, and that source build then fails on C++17. With this row they hit `+cu13torch2.14cxx11abiTRUE` (or `cu12…`) directly.

## What

- `publish.yml`: add `"2.14.0"` to `torch-version`. Exclude `cxx11_abi: FALSE` for it, same as every torch ≥ 2.7 row (PyTorch wheels ship CXX11 ABI = 1, so a FALSE wheel is unusable and would only double the job count). No CUDA exclude is needed: on the 12.9.1 runner the build picks the `cu126` torch wheel, on 13.0.1 the `cu130` one (see next point).
- `_build.yml`: extend the torch-minor → CUDA-tag map that decides which `download.pytorch.org/whl/cuNNN` index to install from ("highest published tag not above the system CUDA"). A missing key is a `KeyError` before torch is even installed, so the matrix row is useless without it. Entries are copied from what PyTorch actually publishes (checked 2026-09-16):

  | torch | published cu tags |
  |---|---|
  | 2.11.0 | 126 128 129 130 |
  | 2.12.x | 126 129 130 132 |
  | 2.13.0 | 126 129 130 132 |
  | 2.14.0 | 126 130 132 (no 128 / 129) |

  Only 2.14 is added to the publish matrix; 2.11–2.13 are in the map so `build.yml` (manual dispatch) can build them on demand.

Matrix cost: +16 jobs (2 OS × 4 Python × 2 CUDA × 1 ABI), 56 → 72 total. aarch64 `manylinux_2_28` wheels for 2.14.0 exist on all three CUDA tags, so the arm runner needs no exclude.

Wheel naming is unchanged: `_build.yml` produces `+cu{12,13}torch2.14cxx11abiTRUE`, which is exactly what `setup.py::get_wheel_url()` computes on the install side (CUDA major only, torch major.minor).

## Verification

- YAML parses; matrix expansion counted by script: 72 jobs, 16 for 2.14.0. `TORCH_CUDA_VERSION` resolves to `cu126` on CUDA 12.9.1 and `cu130` on 13.0.1.
- Local end-to-end on B200 (from reviewing #2879, now merged as f87af617): main + that setup.py change, torch 2.14.0+cu130, `FLASH_ATTN_CUDA_ARCHS=100` — full build 97/97 TUs, 3625-case `tests/test_flash_attn.py` slice passes.
- Suggest one manual `build.yml` dispatch (`ubuntu-22.04`, `3.12`, `13.0.1`, `2.14.0`, `TRUE`) before the next `v*` tag to see a full runner build.

## Not in this PR (maintainer calls)

- Whether to also publish 2.11–2.13 wheels (+16 jobs each) or drop the x86-only 2.6.0 row (−8 jobs) to offset.
- Python 3.14 (torch ≥ 2.10 ships cp314).
- `publish.yml` only runs on `v*` tags, so this catches header changes at release time, not at PR time. A PR-time guard could be a seconds-long CPU job that runs `g++ -fsyntax-only` over `flash_api.cpp`'s torch include set; happy to follow up if wanted.

Related: #2863

title: Build CUDA extension with C++20 on PyTorch 2.13+
body:
## Summary

The NVIDIA CUDA build hardcodes `-std=c++17` for both the host compiler and NVCC. PyTorch 2.13+ requires **C++20** for any extension that includes ATen headers, so building against torch 2.13/2.14 fails at compile time:

```
#error C++20 or later compatible compiler is required to use ATen
```

Because `setup.py` passes an explicit `-std` flag, PyTorch's `cpp_extension` machinery cannot upgrade the standard for us — the hardcoded C++17 forces the failing standard.

Fixes #2863.

## Change

- Select the C++ standard from the installed torch version: `c++20` for `torch >= 2.13`, `c++17` otherwise. Existing toolchains on older torch are unaffected (no regression).
- Applied to both `nvcc_flags` and the host-compiler flags, including the Windows `/std:` variant, so the two stay in sync.
- Renamed `compiler_c17_flag` → `compiler_cxx_flag` since it is no longer always C++17.

The ROCm/HIP build path already uses C++20, so this only aligns the CUDA path.

No kernel implementation or mathematical behavior is changed — this is a build-configuration fix only.

## Testing

- Verified the version-selection logic maps torch `2.12→c++17`, `2.13→c++20`, `2.14→c++20`, `3.x→c++20`.
- The change is confined to the NVIDIA CUDA branch of `setup.py`; `python -m py_compile setup.py` passes.
- Full end-to-end build against torch 2.14 + CUDA 13.2 / SM120 was reported working by the issue author (#2863); I do not have matching CUDA/GPU hardware to re-run the full compile here, so I validated the setup.py logic rather than the produced binary.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

title: [CuTe, SM100] Sparse MLA bwd: in-kernel recompute-P + token-chunked backward
body:
Two composable, opt-in memory features for the sparse top-k MLA (DSA) path. Kwargs-only API; the default path is untouched (same binaries, speed, and memory — sentinel tests pass with and without the flags).

## `gather_bwd_recompute_p=True`

The forward saves only `out` + `lse` — no `p`/`row_max` at all (**508 MiB/1k tokens → 0** of saved activations; train forward 4.43 → 3.77 ms at 8k since the `p` store leaves the softmax critical path; the training forward reuses the inference binary). The backward main kernel reconstructs `P = exp2(scale·log2e·S − lse·log2e)` in-kernel with an extra Sᵀ UMMA over the already-gathered V (+ gathered K_rope for the rope chunk), masking invalid top-k slots on the exponent via the gather bitmask; smem stays at the exact 232448 B SM100 cap (dS merges into sP, sScaleP→sLse, stationary-QvB role swap).

- Forward `out`/`lse`: **bitwise-identical** to the default path.
- Grads: not bitwise (one fewer rounding in P) and measure **more** accurate vs an fp32 reference.
- `retain_graph` is safe: nothing saved is consumed.
- `recompute_P` requires the KV bitmask (asserted — it is the only masking in this mode).

## `gather_bwd_token_chunk=N`

The backward loops its three kernels over token chunks, bounding the p-sized dS transient (~520 KiB/token at H=128, W=2048) by the chunk instead of the sequence. With causal masking the chunked main kernel shrinks its K extent to `seqlen_k − seqlen_q + tok1` per chunk (non-varlen: sliced views; varlen: clamped `cu_seqlens_k` ends) so the recomputed bitmask reproduces the forward's key limit exactly; fully-masked chunks (`k_end ≤ 0`) skip all three kernels and zero their dq/dqv directly. Requires varlen or batch 1; the kwarg is validated at the entry points (positive int; sparse-MLA calls only).

- Chunked dq/dqv: **bitwise-identical** to unchunked (including adversarial non-causal indices under `causal=True`, varlen docs split across chunk boundaries, shared-kv, and rectangular `seqlen_q > seqlen_k`).
- dk/dv: differ only by fp32-atomic accumulation order (≤ the unchunked kernel's own run-to-run noise).

## Results (GB200, B=1, W=2048, bf16, square T=S, train step, median time / peak memory)

All columns H=128 except tilelang finetune, whose backward exceeds SM100 smem at H=128 and runs at H=64 (**half** the head-FLOPs).

| T=S  | FA4 main (H=128)         | tilelang dsv32 (H=128)     | tilelang finetune (H=64)   | this PR (`recompute_p` + `chunk=4096`) | vs main              |
|------|--------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------|
| 4k   | 12.75 ms / 5.14 GiB      | 64.08 ms / 1.08 GiB        | 70.04 ms / 0.55 GiB        | 13.44 ms / 3.08 GiB                    | +5.4% time, −40% mem |
| 8k   | 25.90 ms / 10.28 GiB     | 105.50 ms / 2.16 GiB       | 137.29 ms / 1.09 GiB       | 27.46 ms / 4.15 GiB                    | +6.0%, −60%          |
| 16k  | 53.61 ms / 20.55 GiB     | 188.53 ms / 4.32 GiB       | 272.47 ms / 2.19 GiB       | 56.40 ms / 6.31 GiB                    | +5.2%, −69%          |
| 32k  | 115.58 ms / 41.10 GiB    | 368.55 ms / 8.64 GiB       | 543.30 ms / 4.37 GiB       | 119.68 ms / 10.62 GiB                  | +3.5%, −74%          |
| 64k  | 260.62 ms / 82.20 GiB    | 730.25 ms / 17.27 GiB      | 1094.00 ms / 8.74 GiB      | 262.75 ms / 19.23 GiB                  | +0.8%, −77%          |
| 128k | OOM (186 GiB)            | 1480.45 ms / 34.55 GiB     | 2213.11 ms / 17.48 GiB     | 575.43 ms / 36.47 GiB                  | —                    |

tilelang reference: `tilelang` @ 0.1.13, same machine and methodology, `-1` index tails remapped to 0 (its gathers/scatters are unguarded; identical traffic). dsv32 = `examples/deepseek_v32/sparse_mla_{fwd,bwd}.py` with the head-split backward — same head-FLOPs, the apples-to-apples column: this PR is 4.8× (4k) to 2.6× (128k) faster. finetune = `examples/dsa_sparse_finetune/` at H=64: even at half the head-FLOPs it is ~4× slower than this PR at H=128. Before this PR the tilelang kernels used ~5× less memory than FA4 while being 2.6–5× slower; after it, FA4 matches their memory scaling (285–300 MiB/1k tokens vs dsv32's 270) at the same speed advantage — the remaining ~2 GiB gap at 64k is the chunk-sized dS transient. Full methodology, smem map, and design notes in `AI/SPARSE_MLA_RECOMPUTE_P.md`.

## Robustness hardening included in this PR

- The sV gather stages are zero-filled once at kernel launch: masked top-k slots skip their `cp.async`, so launch-time smem garbage could otherwise reach the dP GEMM as `0 × NaN` (a pre-existing load-p hazard; recompute mode additionally hardens dS against non-finite dP).
- The dV epilogue scatter is bounds-guarded (`0 ≤ idx < seqlen_k`), so chunked-causal runs never write past the sliced dv view (and skip the wasted zero atomics).
- `pipeline_bitmask` gets its `producer_tail` (same invariant the forward documents); the QvB/dO/dOt TMA tx-count invariants are asserted as actually paired; all warps (including the mma warp) use the same static top-k group count.
- One `SharedStorage` struct for all three compile modes via zero-size fields — per-mode layouts byte-identical (verified at 232448 B each).
- The bwd-preprocess compile key distinguishes `lse_log2` presence, so cached binaries can't be reused across mismatched signatures.

## Tests

`tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py -k mla_sparse` (34 cases): recompute-P vs fp32 reference + bitwise-forward checks; chunked-vs-unchunked (recompute and load-p, non-varlen and varlen with docs split across chunks, for both the rope and shared-KV kernel specializations, checked against per-doc fp32 references); fully-masked rows (all `-1` slots: `out = 0`, `lse = −inf`, NaN-free zero grads, unaffected rows bitwise); rectangular `seqlen_q > seqlen_k` chunking (exercises the skip-chunk path); learnable sink + sparse gather in every mode (out/lse/dsink bitwise-identical across default, recompute-P and chunked; all grads incl. dsink vs the fp32 reference — the sink lives inside `lse`, and dsink depends only on the full-size `dpsum`/`lse`, so neither feature needs sink-specific handling); plus the pre-existing sentinel suites with and without the new flags.

title: [FA2, SM89] Add D512 forward and backward
body:
Gemma4-E4B global attention uses `head_dim=512`. FA2 currently rejects it on RTX 4090 with `FlashAttention forward only supports head dimension at most 256`.

This adds native CUDA D512 forward and backward for SM89. It supports FP16/BF16, dense and varlen inputs, MHA/MQA/GQA, causal attention, and deterministic backward. The tiles use 64 KiB shared memory for forward and 96 KiB for backward. The D512 dQ accumulator layout follows its 64-thread MMA layout.

D512 requires zero attention dropout. Local attention, softcap, ALiBi, paged/split KV, `leftpad_k`, `seqused_k`, and `flash_attn_with_kvcache` remain unsupported. Existing head dimensions keep their current paths.

Validation on RTX 4090 (48 GB, SM89), PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128, CUDA 12.8:
- Reproduced the original error with the unchanged upstream API.
- 105 new tests and 56 existing regression cases passed.
- Compute Sanitizer: 0 memory errors and 0 race hazards.
- Real Gemma4-E4B global-layer inputs passed FP64 output and gradient checks. LoRA backward with checkpointing and HF cached decoding also ran successfully.

For BF16, batch 1, Q/KV heads 8/2, causal attention, scale 1.0:

| Tokens | FA2 forward + backward | PyTorch efficient SDPA |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 512 | 0.56 ms | 0.93 ms |
| 2048 | 5.66 ms | 9.00 ms |
| 4096 | 19.11 ms | 22.92 ms |
| 8192 | 73.35 ms | 69.97 ms |

The benchmark includes SDPA KV expansion and gradient reduction. Forward alone is slower. Training uses less extra memory, but the 8192-token case still needs optimization.

Full-model training parity is not established. In a BF16 LoRA probe, the full-model gradient relative L2 difference was about 0.25 against FP32/FP64 global-attention references. FP32 versus FP64 references also differed by 0.245. Deterministic native repeats matched exactly. These are smoke and kernel accuracy checks, not convergence results.

Run `pytest -q tests/test_flash_attn_sm89_d512.py` and `python benchmarks/benchmark_flash_attention_d512.py` after building.

Related to #2581. This PR covers the FA2 training path; paged-KV support requested there remains open.

title: [CuTe, SM100, HD256] optimize SM100 HD256 varlen scheduling and epilogues
body:
## Summary

- Bound dedicated SM100/SM110 HD256 varlen forward, dQ, and dK/dV grids by runtime maximum sequence lengths instead of packed total-token extents.
- Preserve packed output alignment for vector stores.
- Use TMA stores for complete 128-row dQ tiles while retaining predicate stores for ragged tails.
- Add targeted MQA correctness coverage for complete and ragged tiles under causal and noncausal masking.

This closes #2521. Thanks to @horakka5 for the original root-cause analysis and reproducer.

## Why

The dedicated HD256 kernels used the packed `total_q` / `total_k` extents to size each batch's grid. For a packed input with `B` equal-length sequences this launches approximately `B` times more M tiles than necessary, with most CTAs exiting after reading `cu_seqlens`.

After fixing the grid, packed-varlen epilogues become visible in short-sequence profiles:

- Forward used `domain_offset` for the runtime packed-row offset, which discarded the alignment proof needed by `autovec_copy`.
- Backward constructed a dQ TMA destination only for fixed-length inputs. Every varlen dQ tile therefore used the predicate global-store path, including complete tiles that cannot cross a sequence boundary.

The change keeps the physical packed tensor extents unchanged. Runtime maximum sequence lengths are used only for grid sizing. Within a sequence, complete dQ tiles use TMA; the final partial tile keeps the bounds-checked path.

## Benchmark protocol

- GPU: NVIDIA GB200, SM100
- PyTorch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- CUDA: 13.0
- CUTLASS DSL: 4.5.2
- dtype: BF16
- packed-varlen layout: `Q=[B*S,Hq,256]`, `K/V=[B*S,1,256]`
- `Hkv=1`, dropout disabled, softcap disabled
- seed: `20260814`
- `CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS=16`
- 20 warmups per phase
- 5 retained trials; reported latency is the median
- 50 timed iterations per trial for `S <= 8K`, otherwise 20
- FA4 HD256 backward uses `deterministic=False` because the current upstream kernel rejects deterministic mode

The baseline is upstream main before this PR. Commit `0251105` only changes dependency requirements; its HD256 kernels are identical to the measured `145b101` baseline.

MFU uses the repository's historical GB200 roofline:

- compute peak: 2.5 PFLOP/s
- HBM peak: 8 TB/s
- BWD useful FLOPs: `2.5 * FWD FLOPs`
- BWD `exec` is the useful MFU multiplied by 1.4 to reflect the split dQ + dK/dV kernel work

## Forward results

| `(1,128K,1)` | Noncausal | 12.249 ms | 12.217 ms | 1.00x | 57.4% | 57.6% |

## Backward results

BWD MFU is shown as `useful / exec`.

| Shape `(B,S,Hq)` | Mask | Baseline latency | Fixed latency | Speedup | Baseline MFU | Fixed MFU |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `(32,1K,8)` | Causal | 2.033 ms | 0.680 ms | **2.99x** | 6.8% / 9.5% | **20.2% / 28.3%** |

The shape dependence matches the expected mechanism:

- Many short sequences benefit strongly because the old grid multiplies packed totals by batch size.
- At `B=1`, grid sizing is unchanged and attention computation dominates, so differences are within normal run-to-run variation.
- Complete dQ tiles benefit from TMA; only sequence tails retain predicate stores.

title: [CuTe, SM90] hdim256 backward: C++ FA3 dQ path and 2-CTA DSMEM dS exchange (373 → 530 TFLOP/s)
body:
## Summary

This PR takes the CuTe SM90 backward at head_dim 256 from 373 to 530 TFLOP/s (dense bf16, S=16k, H200), 1.42x, past the C++ FA3 kernel (480 TFLOP/s on the same GPU), with unchanged numerics. It is the follow-up to #2888, which fixed the swapped postprocess layout and moved hdim 256 to a 2-stage 64x48 config (302 → 373 TFLOP/s). The two optimization commits are independently useful:

1. **C++ FA3's hdim256 dQ path** (`BwdConfig.dQacc_use_TMA=False`). No smem staging of dQ: the MMA warp groups reduce the dQ accumulator straight into `dQaccum` with `red.global.add.v4.f32`, partitioned by the same R2S tiled copy as the smem path, so the gmem layout and the postprocess are unchanged. dQ is computed in two hdim halves into the same registers (C++ `Slice_dQKV_Mma`; with two accumulators ptxas hoists the second WGMMA above the atomics and dV spills at tile_n=80). The freed 64 KB is what lets the C++ tile (64x80, 2-stage Q) fit. 373 → 471 TFLOP/s, C++ FA3 is 480 on the same GPU.
2. **FA4's 2-CTA dS exchange, on Hopper via DSMEM** (`BwdConfig.cluster_size=2`). With the atomics compiled out the 1-CTA kernel runs at 747 TFLOP/s, so what remains is the fp32 reduce traffic into dQaccum (`S² · d · 4 B / tile_n` per head; a single SM sustains only ~30 GB/s of `red.add`). The two CTAs of a cluster take KV blocks n and n^1 of one head, walk the union of their m-block ranges in lockstep and exchange their dS tiles through distributed shared memory (`cp.async.bulk.shared::cluster`, mbarrier full/empty handshake with remote arrive/expect_tx). CTA r then computes `dQ[:, 128r:128r+128] = dS_own @ K_own[:, half] + dS_peer @ K_peer[:, half]` (K = 2·tile_n) and reduces only its half: half the atomics and half the dQ registers at the same tile_n. Splitting by head-dim halves rather than query rows (FA4's Blackwell variant) needs only the peer's K half (20 KB) in smem, which is what makes 64x80 fit exactly (232,448 B). Q and dO are TMA-multicast to the pair. Odd block counts use a "ghost" partner that participates in every barrier with fully masked columns (dS = 0), flushes its dQ half, and skips the dK/dV epilogue. 471 → 530 TFLOP/s.

The pair's fixed cost only pays off once the m-block loop is long enough, so `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` selects the 2-CTA kernel for `seqlen_q >= 2048` (max_seqlen_q for varlen) and keeps the 1-CTA 64x80 config below (measured crossover, table below). Deterministic and block-sparse backward keep the semaphore-ordered smem-staged path, matching the C++ restriction `Deterministic && kHeadDim < 256`. Forward and hdim ≤ 192 are untouched.

A third commit rounds `seqlen_k_rounded` straight to `n_block_size * cluster_size` instead of fixing up the parity of the n-block count. The old form branched on `max_seqlen_k`, which callers may pass as a device tensor (HF/TE varlen): that synced, and raised `DataDependentOutputException` in the FakeTensorMode compile pass. The rounding is the same value and does not branch. The SM100 2-CTA backward has the same issue; the SM90 cluster config added here reaches it from the varlen path.

New surface: two `BwdConfig` fields (`dQacc_use_TMA`, `cluster_size`) and two `FlashAttentionBackwardSm90` constructor arguments of the same names, both selected in `_tile_size_bwd_sm90` (which gains `deterministic` and `seqlen_q` keyword arguments). No public API change.

## Results

H200 (132 SMs, 227 KB smem; CUDA 12.8, torch 2.10, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1), bf16, backward, ms · TFLOP/s:

| | `main` (before #2888) | #2888 | commit 1 (1-CTA) | commit 2 (2-CTA) | C++ FA3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense S=16384 H=16 D=256 | 36.5 · 302 | 29.5 · 373 | 23.3 · 471 | **20.8 · 530** | 22.9 · 480 |
| dense causal S=16384 | 17.2 · 320 | 14.8 · 370 | 11.9 · 464 | **10.5 · 522** | 11.7 · 471 |
| varlen S=86000 H=32 (#2878) | 1931 · 314 | 1672 · 362 | 1314 · 461 | **1250 · 485** | 1277 · 474 |
| varlen causal S=86000 H=32 | — | 790 · 383 | 659 · 460 | **568 · 534** | 645 · 470 |
| dense S=65536 H=16 | 567 · 310 | 480 · 367 | 383 · 459 | **364 · 483** | 371 · 475 |

Other head dims are untouched (the same kernels compile; hdim 192 GQA works because of #2888). Same GPU, `main` and this branch back to back, S=16384 H=16, dense / causal:

| D | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 128 | 8.86 / 4.48 ms · 620 / 614 TFLOP/s | 8.53 / 4.36 ms · 645 / 631 |
| 192 | 15.72 / 7.93 ms · 525 / 520 | 15.46 / 7.73 ms · 533 / 534 |
| 64 | 4.84 / 2.36 ms · 568 / 583 | 4.70 / 2.36 ms · 584 / 583 |

2-CTA vs 1-CTA (same 64x80 tile, H=16, ms ratio; `bench/crossover_*.log`):

| seqlen | 512 | 1024 | 2048 | 4096 | 8192 | 16384 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dense | 1.02 | 1.03 | 0.91 | 0.91 | 0.92 | 0.83 |
| causal | 1.02 | 1.02 | 0.95 | 0.92 | 0.93 | 0.88 |
| local (1024,1024) | 1.00 | 0.97 | 0.90 | 0.89 | 0.89 | 0.91 |
| local (256,0) | 1.02 | 1.01 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.01 |

## Correctness

- Max error vs an fp32 reference is unchanged from `main` on every path (S=2048: dq/dk/dv 1.33e-3 / 1.16e-3 / 9.14e-4 non-causal, 1.20e-2 / 1.21e-2 / 1.58e-2 causal). dQ stays fp32-accumulated; only the reduction order changes, as in the C++ kernel.
- Checked vs the fp32 reference on both the 1-CTA and the 2-CTA kernel: dense, causal, GQA 16/4 and 16/2, MQA, local (200,0)/(100,50)/(256,0)/(1024,1024), softcap, deterministic (bitwise-identical repeat, MHA and GQA; smem path), hdim_v=128, hdim 200/224/240 (MHA and GQA, per kv head), odd n-block counts (ghost CTA), ragged S=1000, S=4096, varlen S=86000.
- Varlen with the 2-CTA kernel, per batch vs the fp32 reference (`bench/varlen_gqa_cluster.py`): GQA/MQA/MHA with batches of 0, 1, odd and many KV blocks, causal and not, identical errors to the 1-CTA kernel (this caught a padded-offset mismatch between the kernel and the dK/dV accumulator layout during review; fixed in commit 2).
- Varlen callers that pass `max_seqlen` as a device tensor: same gradients as the host-int call, and the FakeTensorMode compile pass goes through (commit 3).
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_output -k -256-` (8560 ids: every head_dim 256 case and every seqlen 256 case, mha/mqa/gqa × causal × local × softcap × deterministic × sink): 5246 passed, 3312 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are the `dSink` tolerance check at `[256-256-128-...-mqa]` (diff 0.0018 vs tolerance 0.0011, head_dim 128) and fail identically with `main`'s `flash_bwd_sm90.py` / `interface.py` on this GPU. `test_flash_attn_varlen_output` d=256 random sample (320 ids): 196 passed, 124 skipped, 0 failed. `test_flash_attn_sm90_hdim_padding*` and the empty-workload backward tests: 170 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (0.11.13) clean on `flash_bwd_sm90.py`.

Related: #2878, #2888.

title: [CuTe, Fwd] Fix PackGQA predication for padded head dimensions
body:
## Summary

Fix the CuTe PackGQA load/store predicates for head dimensions that are 8-byte-vector aligned but not multiples of 16 elements, such as 72, 88, 104, 120, and 136.

PackGQA slices Q loads and O stores into one K group. The sliced copy operand retains its vector layout, while the old predicate contains only one Boolean transaction value. CuTe IR verification therefore rejects the default GQA path.

Representative main failures:

- `D=72, Dv=64`: expected predicate shape `((8),(1))`, got `(1,(1))`;
- `D=64, Dv=72`: expected predicate shape `((8,1),(1))`, got `(1,(1))`.

The patch materializes a Boolean fragment matching the sliced operand and fills it with the existing transaction predicate. The branch is compile-time eliminated when no head-dimension predicate is needed.

## Correctness coverage

RTX 5090 / SM120:

- unmodified main: the first three representative dense cases fail during IR verification;
- patch: 25 focused real-GPU cases pass;
- patch: 24 dense FakeTensor compile cases pass;
- BF16 and FP16;
- causal and non-causal;
- `D/Dv` combinations `(72,64)`, `(64,72)`, `(88,88)`, `(104,104)`, `(120,120)`, and `(136,136)`;
- varlen coverage and FP32-reference numerical checks;
- tests exercise the public default dispatch, where GQA automatically selects PackGQA.

## RTX 5090 performance

BF16/FP16, batch 1, 8 Q heads / 1 KV head, D=72. Each cell uses seven alternating unpacked/PackGQA timing blocks with 50 launches per block. Values are `pack_gqa=False latency / PackGQA latency`; greater than 1 means PackGQA is faster.

| dtype | sequence | non-causal | causal |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| BF16 | 512 | 1.052x | 0.997x |
| BF16 | 2048 | 1.003x | 0.967x |
| BF16 | 8192 | 1.002x | 1.125x |
| FP16 | 512 | 1.064x | 0.998x |
| FP16 | 2048 | 1.004x | 0.967x |
| FP16 | 8192 | 1.001x | 1.168x |

The 12-cell geometric mean is 1.027x. The optimization is shape-dependent: causal S2048 is about 3.3% slower, while causal S8192 is 12.5%-16.8% faster. This PR's primary capability is making the already-selected default PackGQA path compile and run for these dimensions; it does not claim a universal speedup.

## Related work and scope

#2634 introduced related full-fragment predicates in partial-row PackGQA branches. Its current tile-aligned generic path still retains the compressed predicate and reproduces this padded-dimension failure, so the focused fix remains independently useful.

The global predicate helper, TMA paths, pointer/layout mapping, and backward kernels are intentionally unchanged.

title: [CuTe, Bwd] Return zero gradients for empty Q/K workloads
[CuTe, SM90] Fix swapped backward MMA layout and use 2-stage hdim256 config
body:
## Summary

SM90 backward at head_dim 256 runs at ~300 TFLOP/s while hdim 128 is at parity with the C++ FA3 kernel (#2878). The cause is the hdim 256 config: it is the only SM90 backward config with `num_stages_Q=1`, so the Q/dO TMA loads and the WGMMAs are serialized every m-block. The C++ tile (64x80, 2-stage Q) does not fit next to the 64 KB smem dQaccum staging buffer, but 64x48 with `dKV_swapAB` does.

Using that config for GQA/MQA as well needs one real fix, and it turned up a second one:

1. **Swapped dK/dV postprocess layout.** `FlashAttentionBackwardPostprocess._get_tiled_mma` reversed the whole `(tile / atom_layout)` tiler for `swap_ab`, which asks `make_trivial_tiled_mma` for a WGMMA atom with M = hdim / num_wg. Every SM90 config with `dKV_swapAB` therefore fails in the GQA/MQA postprocess: `expects the M-mode to be 64, but got 192` for hdim in (128, 192] on `main` today (cf. #2087), `got 128` for `dQ_swapAB` above hdim 128. Build the tiled MMA the way the mainloop does, `tiler_mn=(64, tile / atom_layout on N)`; the accumulator register layout is unchanged.
2. **GQA dV accumulator rounding.** `dv_accum` was allocated with a fixed 32-element head-dim rounding while the kernel and the postprocess use `hdim_multiple_of` (64 with `dKV_swapAB`), so head_dim_v in {160, 200, 208, 224} reduced and read past each (batch, kv-head) region and dV came out wrong. Round it like `dk_accum`.
3. **hdim 256 config: 64x48, 2-stage Q, `dKV_swapAB`**, the same for MHA, GQA and MQA (no per-mode fallback). `dKV_swapAB` rounds `tile_hdim` to 64, so head_dim in (192, 256) (200/208/224/240, which currently abort inside the DSL compiler or fail in `get_smem_store_C`) now compiles and is correct. Block-sparse backward keeps the previous 64x64 tile because it derives its KV block size from `n_block_size`.

No new kernel or config parameters; forward and hdim <= 192 configs are untouched. 3 files, +40/-9 including tests.

## Results

H20Z (H200 silicon, 132 SMs, 227 KB smem; CUDA 12.8, torch 2.10, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1), bf16, backward:

| | `main` (8d3a3b8) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| dense S=16384 H=16 D=256 | 36.5 ms · 302 TFLOP/s | **29.5 ms · 373** |
| dense causal S=16384 H=16 D=256 | 17.2 ms · 320 | **14.8 ms · 370** |
| varlen S=86000 H=32 D=256 (the shape in #2878) | 1931 ms · 314 | **1672 ms · 362** |
| varlen causal S=86000 H=32 D=256 | — | 790 ms · 383 |
| GQA hdim 192, hdim 200/208/224/240 | fail | work |

The remaining gap to C++ FA3 (~480 TFLOP/s here) is the smem dQaccum staging; that is a separate, larger change (C++ FA3's `dQacc_use_TMA=false` path) and will be a follow-up PR.

## Correctness

- Max error vs an fp32 reference (S=2048) is unchanged from `main`: dq/dk/dv 1.33e-3 / 1.16e-3 / 9.14e-4 non-causal, 1.20e-2 / 1.21e-2 / 1.58e-2 causal (identical numbers on `main`).
- Checked vs the fp32 reference: dense, causal, GQA 16/4, GQA causal 16/2, MQA, local (200,0) and (100,50), softcap, deterministic (bitwise-identical repeat, MHA and GQA), hdim_v=128, hdim 200/224/240 for MHA and GQA (per kv head), ragged S=1000, S=4096.
- `tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py::test_flash_attn_output`, d=256 subset (seqlen pairs 1-1 / 128-128 / 113-203 / 256-512 / 384-256 / 799-3 × causal × local_enum × softcap × deterministic × learnable_sink × mha/mqa/gqa, 1152 ids): **720 passed, 432 skipped (local+causal combinations the test skips), 0 failed**.
- `test_flash_attn_sm90_hdim_padding*` (this PR extends `d` to 200/224/240 and adds a GQA variant for d = 160/192/224): **150 passed** (was 96 cases on `main`, where the new ones fail).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` (v0.11.13, as in pre-commit) clean on the CI-covered file.

Fixes #2878. Related: #2087.

title: [Cute,Fwd,Sm100] S/P ping-pong to overlap QK with softmax in decode
body: This PR adds an S/P ping-pong to the SM100 forward kernel for single and multi-token decode (`q_stage=1`): the MMA warp overlaps QK for block i+1 with the softmax and correction of block i. Previously, the MMA warp had to wait for softmax warps to drain S, write P, and for correction warps to rescale O before it could issue the next QK. The original kernel allocated two S/P TMEM slots at `q_stage=1` with the second slot unused. This change takes advantage of that vacant TMEM slot to implement the ping-pong. A new pipeline depth attribute `s_p_o_stage` is introduced that is equal to 2 when S/P ping-pong is enabled and is equal to `q_stage` otherwise. The K/V load order is changed to "K0, K1, V0, K2, V1, K3,..." to match the order of the matmuls. Disabled with `FA_DISABLE_S_PING_PONG=1`. Currently gated to: `q_stage=1`, hdim 64/128 with `head_dim_v == head_dim`, 128x128 tiles, no 2-CTA, no score mod/mask mod, no block sparsity, no learnable sink, contiguous KV or paged KV with page_size == 128, and num_splits=1 or the number of KV blocks per split is at least 16 for hdim 64 and at least 64 for hdim 128. title: Codex/fix windows msvc linker
[CuTe, SM100] Support 1..128 Q heads in sparse MLA via in-kernel TMA padding
body:
## Human Note

Support [1, 128] Q heads in the public sparse MLA (DSA) forward and backward paths. I saw that there was a comment for supporting n_qheads = 64 not sure if you planned to do something fancier here. I did the easy thing (just pad out).  This does infact come up both for dsv4 flash and when doing tp sharding. I found this when trying to integrate into torchtitan. I consider this a naive unblock but it does help :)


I thought about the multi tokens e.g. true pack-gqa but didnt want to visit the union + masking (although ill prototype this) -> same reason why I didnt support this for blocksparse impl

## Agent Notes
TMA pads heads inside the kernel without padded operand copies in global memory. This enables training with 64-head models and tensor-parallel shards.

Each forward tile still covers one token and one top-k gather list: 2-CTA UMMA, 128 packed Q heads, 64 rows per CTA, with K/V split across the pair. Backward uses a 64- or 128-head tile. The dQ/dQv GEMM keeps its 128-row tile with a dynamic head extent.

Unchanged: attention math, the 128-head TMA path, MMA tile sizes, and pipeline synchronization.

### Mechanism

- `padded_qheads_tma_source` builds a heads-first view `(h, d, s, b)` with a dynamic head extent, so CuTe tiles it without requiring divisibility. TMA zero-fills out-of-bounds loads and drops out-of-bounds stores. `regroup_padded_qheads` restores the packed coordinate layout `((tile, s), d, 1, b)`.
- LSE, row_max, and learnable-sink accesses guard the packed head index. Without guards, the hierarchical packed layout wraps padded heads into the next token.
- TMA loads zero padded Q rows in forward and dO/P rows in backward. These rows produce `dS = 0` and contribute nothing to dK/dV. Only `scaleP`/`dPsum` need tile-width global buffers with finite padding.

### Two latent bugs

1. **Backward dV staging at `tile_m=64`.** The split-0 epilogue could overwrite dOt/Qvt operands still used by the split-1 MMA, producing NaNs in `dV[:, 256:]`. If staging equals one operand stage, each split now stages in place over its consumed stage. Otherwise, both splits take turns using one staging area allocated after the operands.
2. **Non-power-of-two preprocess tiles.** A 48-row tile (2 tokens × 24 heads) produced incorrect `dpsum`. Padded head counts now use trivial packing (`qhead_per_kvhead=1, nheads_kv=H`) with the existing 128-row tile. Not all head counts divide that tile; resizing it to a non-power-of-two is not a valid workaround.

### Validation (GB200)

- Sentinel-focused run: 44 passed. `test_flash_attn_mla_sparse_bwd_sentinel` covers H ∈ {128, 64, 96, 24, 1} × shared_kv × causal × 2 lengths.
- `test_flash_attn_mla_absorbed`: 96 BF16 cases passed for `1024-1024` and `255-1025`, including the 128-head path.
- Probe against global-memory padding to 128 heads, H ∈ {1, 8, 16, 24, 48, 64, 72, 96, 100, 120}: out/LSE/P/row_max/dQ/dQv bit-identical; dK/dV within 1e-5.

### Performance at DeepSeek-V4 shapes

Measurement contract: GB200, B=1, D_qk = D_v = 512, shared KV, sliding window 128 + compressed causal top-k, via attention-gym `selected_attention`. Flash uses top-k 512; pro uses top-k 1024. Times are medians over CUDA-graph replays, in µs per call (lower is better). Peak memory is MB (lower is better).

Calculated rates (higher is better): fwd FLOPs = 2*T*H*K*(D_qk + D_v), K = valid gathered slots (top-k + window); bwd FLOPs = 2.5× fwd. TB/s counts gathered KV rows plus Q read and O write.

| T | config | fwd us | fwd TFLOPS | fwd TB/s | bwd us | bwd TFLOPS | fwd+bwd us | peak MB |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 | flash H=64 in-kernel pad | 859 | 400 | 3.75 | 1874 | 458 | 2733 | 2114 |
| 4096 | flash H=64 gmem pad->128 | 1061 | 324 | 3.04 | 2835 | 303 | 3896 | 4557 |
| 4096 | H=128, flash topk 512 | 918 | 749 | 4.10 | 2465 | 697 | 3382 | 4046 |
| 4096 | pro H=128 topk 1024 | 1349 | 917 | 4.38 | 3798 | 814 | 5147 | 5109 |
| 8192 | flash H=64 in-kernel pad | 1666 | 412 | 3.87 | 3702 | 464 | 5368 | 4095 |
| 8192 | H=128, flash topk 512 | 1775 | 774 | 4.24 | 4876 | 705 | 6651 | 7959 |
| 8192 | pro H=128 topk 1024 | 2650 | 933 | 4.46 | 7539 | 820 | 10189 | 10087 |
| 16384 | flash H=64 in-kernel pad | 3293 | 417 | 3.91 | 7347 | 468 | 10640 | 8061 |
| 16384 | H=128, flash topk 512 | 3506 | 784 | 4.29 | 9723 | 707 | 13229 | 15789 |
| 16384 | pro H=128 topk 1024 | 5262 | 940 | 4.49 | 15029 | 823 | 20292 | 20045 |

At T=4096, H=64 in-kernel padding reduces fwd+bwd time by about 30% and peak memory by about half versus global-memory padding. H=64 forward takes about 93% of the H=128 time. NCU on the H=64 forward (T=4096): DRAM throughput 8%, L2 hit rate 74%, 74% of stall cycles are long-scoreboard waits on the per-thread cp.async gather. The forward is gather-latency-bound, so the padded MMA rows cost little; the gather itself is the lever for a follow-up.

Separate T=2048 comparison: GB200, top-k 512, D=512, fwd+bwd via attention-gym `selected_attention`; time in µs per call (lower is better).

| Configuration | fwd+bwd us |

| Native H=128 | 1740 |

title: [CuTe, SM100] hd256 2-CTA: support seqused_q/seqused_k and the decoder paged-KV shape
body:
## Problem

The dedicated SM100/SM110 head-dim 256 2-CTA forward kernel asserts off per-batch actual
sequence lengths:

```
AssertionError: SM100 forward with head_dim=256 does not support seqused_q/seqused_k
```

`seqused_k` is exactly what continuous-batching inference servers supply for decoder
attention over a paged KV cache. As a direct consequence, vLLM disabled FA4 head-dim 256
on Blackwell entirely on 2026-08-16 (vllm-project/vllm#52050, "[Bugfix] Temporarily
disable FA4 head-dim 256"), stating:

> PR #42669 enabled FA4 head-dim 256 on Blackwell, but the specialized SM100 2-CTA kernel
> still rejects `seqused_q/k`, which vLLM decoder attention supplies. Temporarily resolve
> FA2 for head-dim 256 on Blackwell until upstream adds the required support. FA4 remains
> enabled for head-dim 128 and the supported MLA 192/128 case.

This PR implements that support in the forward kernel, and adapts the adjacent paged-KV
calling contract that blocks the same path, so head-dim 256 models can run FA4 on
Blackwell under continuous batching again.

## What changed

**`flash_attn/cute/sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_forward.py`**

The dedicated kernel does not use `SeqlenInfoQK`; it threads per-work-tile
`seqlen_q`/`seqlen_k` scalars inline into `FusedMask.get_trip_start_count_via_block_info`
and the epilogue/LSE predication. This change keeps that inline convention and overrides
the two scalars with the per-batch `seqused` values at the four work-tile setup sites
(load, MMA, softmax, correction/epilogue), with the same precedence
`SeqlenInfoQK.create` implements in the general SM100 kernel:

- `seqused_q`/`seqused_k` win for the *lengths*;
- `cu_seqlens_q`/`cu_seqlens_k` continue to provide the packing *offsets*.

Two properties the placement guarantees:

- **Warp lockstep.** When `seqused_q` shrinks a batch below a q tile, the work-skip
  predicate (`continue_cond`) is recomputed with the identical expression in every warp
  section, so the load, MMA, softmax and correction pipelines agree on which work tiles
  are skipped (same discipline as the varlen `cu_seqlens_q` path today).
- **No new out-of-bounds exposure.** `seqused_* <= ` allocated lengths only ever *shrink*
  trip counts relative to the existing static/varlen values; tail positions inside the
  last KV tile are masked to exact-zero probability exactly as the varlen path already
  does. Zero-length batches ride the existing zero-trip clamp.

The `mSeqUsedQ`/`mSeqUsedK` parameters already existed in `__call__` for interface parity
(marked TODO); they are now forwarded into the device kernel. The interface compile key
already contained `seqused_q is None` / `seqused_k is None`, so the no-seqused
specialization is byte-identical to before — **zero impact when seqused is not passed**
(all new device code is behind `cutlass.const_expr`).

**`flash_attn/cute/interface.py`**

- Remove the `seqused_q is None and seqused_k is None` assert from the
  `use_dedicated_hd256_kernel` forward branch. The surrounding plumbing (tensor
  normalization, compile args, call args, compile key) already passed seqused through;
  only the assert blocked it.
- Add one loud guard: `cu_seqlens_k` without `cu_seqlens_q` is rejected for this kernel.
  The dedicated kernel derives its K/V load offsets from the varlen-Q block, so
  varlen-packed K without varlen Q would read every batch from offset 0 (silently wrong).
  This mode was previously unreachable only because the seqused assert happened to block
  the test path into it; with seqused enabled it must be rejected explicitly. (No known
  caller uses this combination; vLLM uses `cu_seqlens_q` + `page_table` + `seqused_k`.)

**`flash_attn/cute/interface.py` — paged-KV extent/page-table contract**

Removing the `seqused` assert alone does *not* re-open the decoder path, because the same
branch also asserts, for paged KV:

```python
assert max_seqlen_k % page_size == 0
assert page_table.shape[1] == max_seqlen_k // page_size
```

(pre-existing code, not introduced here — its own message tells the caller to
`pass page_table[:, :N]`). A continuous-batching decoder cannot satisfy either one:
`max_seqlen_k` is the *current batch maximum* sequence length, which is arbitrary and
rarely a multiple of the page size, and `page_table` has a fixed width sized for the
largest supported context, independent of the current batch. In vLLM's decoder call
these come straight from the batch metadata (`seqused_k = seq_lens`,
`max_seqlen_k = max_seq_len` — the batch max — and `block_table`, the full-width table).
So a decode step with, say, `max_seqlen_k = 257` and a 256-column table trips both
asserts even with `seqused_k` support in place.

This PR therefore normalizes the two values in the interface instead of requiring the
caller to pre-slice: round the KV extent up to the enclosing page and narrow the table to
match.

```python
required_pages = (max_seqlen_k + page_size - 1) // page_size
assert page_table.shape[1] >= required_pages      # genuinely-too-small table: still loud
page_table = page_table[:, :required_pages]
max_seqlen_k = required_pages * page_size
```

Three properties worth checking in review:

- **Placement.** It runs *before* `_get_fwd_config`, before the compile key, and before
  the page-table tensor conversion, so tile selection, kernel specialization and the
  device-side tensor all see the same normalized values. (`max_seqlen_k` reaches the
  compile key indirectly, through the tile sizes `_get_fwd_config` picks.)
- **Rounding is bounded by `seqused_k`, and that is enforced.** Widening the extent is
  only faithful to the caller if each sequence is still bounded at its true length.
  `seqused_k` is that bound — positions in `[seqused_k, rounded)` mask to exact-zero
  probability, exactly like the existing intra-tile tail. If `max_seqlen_k` needs
  rounding and no `seqused_k` is given, the interface now refuses loudly rather than
  silently letting every sequence attend the remainder of its last page. The kernel side
  is consistent by construction: it derives its paged extent as
  `mPageTable.shape[1] * page_size`, which is exactly the normalized `max_seqlen_k`.
- **No behavior change for callers that already met the contract.** When `max_seqlen_k`
  is page-aligned and the table is exactly `max_seqlen_k // page_size` wide,
  `required_pages` equals the existing width, the slice is a no-op and the extent is
  unchanged — the existing paged hd256 tests are bit-identical.

This is a deliberate contract change: it moves the slicing from the caller into the
interface. The argument for it is that the contract as written cannot be met by the
consumer this kernel exists to serve, and the normalization is exactly the slice the
assert message already asks for. If you would rather keep the contract caller-side, the
alternative is a documented helper plus a change on the vLLM side; happy to go that way
instead.

The head-dim 256 **backward** still rejects `seqused_q/seqused_k` (unchanged); forward
inference is what unblocks the serving use case.

## Tests

**`tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py`**

- `test_flash_attn_varlen_output`: drop the d=256 skip of the seqused modes
  (`unpad_q/unpad_kv = False`). The existing matrix now exercises, for hd256:
  per-batch random lengths, `seqused_q`-only, `seqused_k`-only, both, zero-length
  batches, seqused == full length (`varlen_mode="full"`), across the existing
  seqlen/causal/GQA/dtype grid — all against the PyTorch reference. The backward leg
  stays restricted to the fully-unpadded mode (hd256 backward does not support seqused
  yet); a narrow skip remains for the unsupported varlen-K-without-varlen-Q combination,
  matching the new interface guard.
- New `test_flash_attn_paged_hd256_sm100_tma_seqused_k` (mirrors the existing
  `test_flash_attn_paged_hd256_sm100_tma*` family): paged KV with a `page_table` wider
  than the batch needs and per-batch `seqused_k` of {page-aligned, one past a page
  boundary, mid-page}, for q=1 (decode) and q>1, parametrized over both callers —
  `max_seqlen_k` as the **batch maximum** (257: neither page-aligned nor equal to
  `page_table.shape[1] * page_size`, the shape the decoder actually passes, and the case
  that fails without the normalization above) and `max_seqlen_k` page-aligned at the
  allocated capacity (what a caller that pre-slices passes). Both are checked against a
  dense varlen reference over the true per-batch lengths. Everything past each
  sequence's `seqused_k` — the tail inside its last page and every page after it — is
  poisoned with large finite values, and the test asserts the output is finite and stays
  within the reference's magnitude range, so a leak past `seqused_k` (e.g. if the rounded
  extent were not masked) fails loudly instead of drifting. Finite poison rather than
  NaN is deliberate: masked positions still contribute `0 * value` to the PV
  accumulation, so `0 * NaN` would poison a correct kernel too.
  `seqused_k == allocated length` is asserted **bitwise identical** to not passing
  `seqused_k`.
- New `test_flash_attn_paged_hd256_sm100_tma_contract_guards`: asserts both normalization
  guards fire — a `page_table` too narrow for the requested extent, and an extent that
  needs rounding with no `seqused_k` to bound the sequences.

## Testing done / not done

- Static validation of this branch: `py_compile`, AST-level checks of the four device
  sites, launch/signature ordering against the interface compile/call argument order.
- **Run on B300 (SM103) hardware against this exact source**, covering the decoder shapes
  this PR is about:

  | case | result |
  |---|---|
  | `max_seqlen_k=257` (batch max, not page-aligned) against a full four-column page table — the shape the old assert rejected | pass, max err vs fp32 ref `1.95e-3` |
  | page-aligned capacity path | pass, and bit-identical to the current-max output |
  | `q=120` paged causal | pass, max err `7.81e-3` |
  | CUDA Graph captured at KV length 64, replayed after `seqused_k` grew to 129 | pass, max err `1.95e-3` |

  Errors are at the bf16 floor for these shapes.
- A functionally equivalent patch (same per-batch overrides at the same four work-tile
  sites) has additionally been exercised at length on SM103 under vLLM with paged KV
  (page size 128), q=1 decode and prefill — but against vLLM's vendored
  `vllm-flash-attn` copy, which has diverged from this repo.
- **Not covered:** the zero-length paged-KV edge was not executed on hardware. It is not
  part of the decoder contract this PR targets (vLLM does not issue zero-length KV in this
  path), and the kernel's existing zero-trip clamp and zero/NaN `row_sum` guards are what
  make it well-defined — but it is a hardening case rather than a validated one. Narrowing
  the test skip also means the varlen suite now runs `seqused_k` together with zero-length
  sequences for the first time; that is the case I would watch first in CI.

## Relationship to #2749

Semantically orthogonal: #2749 enables causal-left local attention for this same kernel
by removing the adjacent `is_local`/`window_size` asserts; this PR does not touch those
asserts, and neither feature depends on the other. A trial merge of the two branches
shows `sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_forward.py` merges clean; `interface.py` and the test
skip block conflict textually (both PRs edit adjacent lines), which is a few-line
resolution for whichever lands second. The combination (per-batch `seqused_k` +
causal-left sliding window) has been exercised together on SM103, so the two features are
known to compose.

title: [CuTe, SM100] Stop the non-causal hdim 128 softmax warps spilling
body:
## Summary

Register budget for the non-causal hdim 128 (2-CTA) SM100 forward config. The softmax warps get 176 registers there (the causal, 1-CTA config gets 192), and on current `main` that build spills in the softmax hot loop: 21 `LDL` and 18 `STL` per KV block per warp (ncu `--set full`, SASS view, `launch__registers_per_thread` 128 with `setmaxnreg` redistribution). Moving 8 registers from the correction warps to the softmax warps (176/88 -> 184/80, other warps unchanged at 64) removes every spill.

An earlier revision of this PR also added a scheduling fence after the softmax stats arrive; it was dropped per review since it does not measurably help on `main`.

title: Add trainable ALiBi slopes to FA2 CUDA backward
body:
FA2 currently accepts ALiBi slopes in forward but does not return their gradients. This adds FP32 slope gradients to all six training APIs, including when Q/K/V are frozen, addressing [#1977](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/issues/1977).

The CUDA backward accumulates distance-weighted dS before the softcap derivative, with dropout scaling and fixed-order reduction. Variable-length attention sizes temporary storage by actual key tokens. A separate template specialization keeps gradient computation out of frozen-slopes kernels. The native backward retains its four return values and accepts an optional gradient output buffer. Empty Q/K paths return zero gradients.

Validation on RTX 4090, CUDA 13.0 and PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130: 78 tests pass across d32 (2), d64 (74), and d128 (2). Coverage includes the six APIs, FP16/BF16, GQA, local/causal attention, softcap, dropout, deterministic gradients, saved-tensor version checks, actual Inductor fullgraph training, and ragged-memory bounds. Sixteen additional native boundary probes pass. Exact baseline passes four QKV controls and fails twelve slope-gradient cases because slopes are absent from the autograd graph.

Same-lock CUDA Graph ABBA across six BF16 d64 configurations measures frozen-path differences from −0.049% to +0.343%. These are scoped sm89 native builds using all sixteen CUDA source files per head dimension and a scratch API dispatch restriction; C++20 is used for the installed PyTorch. The full distribution build, other GPU architectures, and ROCm slope gradients are outside this validation.

AI-assisted.

title: [FA2] Fix varlen GQA fast path with zero-length queries
body:
## Problem

`flash_attn_varlen_func` fails for GQA when `max_seqlen_q == 1` and a query sequence is empty, such as query lengths [0, 1]. See #1619.

## Root cause

The swapped GQA fast path assumes exactly one query token per batch element. For packed varlen input, `max_seqlen_q == 1` permits zero-length sequences and does not imply that the packed query token count equals batch_size.

The fast path therefore attempts to reshape Q using `batch_size`, which fails when `total_q < batch_size`.

## Fix

Require the original packed Q token count, `sizes[0]`, to equal batch_size before enabling the swapped GQA optimization.

Batches containing empty query sequences fall back to the normal varlen GQA path, while ordinary one-token-per-sequence decoding remains eligible for the fast path.

## Tests

Validated on NVIDIA L4 with PyTorch 2.6.0 and CUDA 12.4:

- Upstream `9d61d35` reproduces the expected invalid reshape.
- Patched `[0, 1]` reproducer passes its numerical check.
- New reference-based regression passes for fp16 and bf16: 2 passed.
- Normal `[1, 1]` GQA sanity check passes, confirming the fast path remains valid.

Validation used a temporary d64 forward-only FA2 build to reduce compilation time. The committed regression test was run unchanged; broader suites were not run.

title: [CuTe, SM103] Add BF16 head-dim 512 paged SplitKV decode
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a narrow FA4 CuTeDSL decode adapter for SM103 with the following
contract:

- BF16 Q/K/V and output;
- Q1, 32 query heads, 4 KV heads, head dimension 512;
- packed HND page-64 KV cache;
- causal full attention;
- up to 32 KV splits.

The producer partitions the KV range across CTAs and writes FP32 output/LSE
partials. A warp-cooperative combine kernel performs the stable log-sum-exp
reduction and writes BF16 output. The adapter validates device, dtype, shape,
stride, page-table, and workspace contracts before compilation. It caches the
compiled CuTe specialization and rejects cold compilation during CUDA Graph
capture.

This does not change the existing public `flash_attn_func` dispatch and does
not claim support for the class's internal page-128, NHD, or dense branches.
The intended first consumer is an inference integration that imports the
narrow adapter directly and retains its existing fallback for all unmatched
calls.

Related: #2456.

## Correctness and graph validation

Tested on one NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, compute capability 10.3, against commit
`792115567cf00f3b96d3697954899f9e63996702` on main
`ce088ab9ce0fc0434dcd8afa0a791da9fcc3a820`.

```text
5 passed, 415818 deselected, 40 warnings in 35.32s
```

The focused cells cover K11, K129, K1024, K4096, and heterogeneous B2
sequence lengths `(11, 129)`. A separate regression matrix passed B1/B4/B8
ragged eager execution and CUDA Graph replay with K mutations from 63 through
8192. The modules also import successfully from
`vllm.vllm_flash_attn.cute.*`, validating the relative combine import used by
vendoring integrations.

Standard focused command:

```bash
pytest -vv -x tests/cute/test_flash_attn.py \
  -k sm103_hd512_splitkv_packed_hnd_adapter
```

The recorded archive run used a small package bootstrap because the archive
did not contain the separately built FA2 `flash_attn_2_cuda` extension that
the repository's top-level initializer imports. The bootstrap changed only
package loading; it passed the same test file and selection shown above.

## Performance

Same-input CUDA Graph replay, BF16, B1/Q1, page 64, three rounds of 500
replays; medians are microseconds per attention call:

| KV length | This PR | FlashInfer TRTLLM-gen | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 65 | 8.202 | 8.200 | 1.000x |
| 512 | 8.201 | 12.290 | 1.499x |
| 1024 | 9.599 | 14.346 | 1.495x |
| 2048 | 10.243 | 14.337 | 1.400x |
| 4096 | 10.260 | 14.350 | 1.399x |
| 8192 | 12.831 | 16.388 | 1.277x |

These numbers measure only the maintained attention-call contract; they are
not whole-model tokens-per-second claims.

## Scope and follow-up

- The adapter is intentionally strict and fail closed.
- General D512 prefill, NHD, page-128, other head counts, and other dtypes are

- The consumer-side dispatch and fallback integration will be submitted
  separately after this kernel is available in its vendored dependency. That
  integration is tracked in
  [vllm-project/vllm#55017](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55017).

title: [CuTe, SM100] Speed up hdim-128 causal forward scheduling
body:
Four scheduling changes to optimize the SM100 forward kernel (head_dim=128, fp16, causal). We trace FA-4 against cuDNN's SDPA at shapes where cuDNN led. We collect these traces using [G-Watch Xtrace](https://g-watch.github.io/en/open-traces/). ## What the traces show

Top row: the SM each CTA was resident on. Bottom row: the warp-role timeline of one SM. At this head dim both kernels use enough SMEM to allow only one resident CTA per SM, so a grid wider than the SM count is serialized into waves. cuDNN is persistent at 148 CTAs; `main` launches one CTA per work tile, so it retires in two waves and idles across the boundary. This PR makes FA-4 persistent at 148 CTAs as well. ## Performance

| shape | `main` | cuDNN | this PR | vs `main` | vs cuDNN | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `b8 h8 s1024` | 770 TFLOP/s | 821 | **864** | **+12.3%** | **+5.2%** | | `b8 h16 s1024` | 737 | 833 | **832** | **+12.8%** | -0.1% | | `b4 h32 s1024` | 735 | 831 | **833** | **+13.3%** | **+0.2%** | | `b2 h16 s4096` | 1336 | 1404 | **1406** | **+5.2%** | **+0.1%** | Output is bitwise identical to `main` at every shape. The first three changes apply to the CLC schedule, which `main` already selects through the existing `FA_CLC` environment variable; the fourth needs no flag. ## Optimization 1: apply the L2 swizzle to the CLC schedule

**Bottleneck.** One CTA per work tile gives a 512-CTA grid over 148 SMs, tail wave dispatched at 84% of the kernel. CLC makes it persistent but returns raw grid coordinates, bypassing the L2 swizzle: alone it reaches only 1149 TFLOP/s at `b2 h16 s4096`, below `main`'s 1336. **Change.** Linearize the CLC coordinate and decode it through the swizzle the static path uses, in `SingleTileLPTScheduler.clc_work_to_coords`. **Result.** `b8 h16 s1024` goes 737 → 806 TFLOP/s. ## Optimization 2: order tiles over the whole problem

**Bottleneck.** The longest-resident CTA sets the kernel duration. The longest-processing-time order is applied per L2 section, so a section narrower than the problem issues every section's heaviest tile at once, leaving 1.49x residency variation. **Change.** Order across the whole problem when it fits one section (`lpt_global`). **Result.** Variation falls to 1.20x. `b8 h16 s1024` goes 806 → 822 TFLOP/s, `b2 h16 s4096` 1257 → 1393. ## Optimization 3: release the output buffer only when an iteration follows **Bottleneck.** Each tile drains its output TMA store and returns the SMEM buffer to the correction warps. On a CTA's final tile neither is required, and a span over that drain measures 544 ns per CTA. cuDNN peels its final iteration instead: its epilogue warps each record one more loop entry than exit. **Change.** Move the `cp_async_bulk_wait_group` and the release past `advance_to_next_work`, predicated on the next tile being valid, dropping the correction warps' tail acquire. **Result.** Every shape gains. `b8 h16 s1024` goes 822 → 832 TFLOP/s. ## Optimization 4: use the static schedule at two or fewer tiles per CTA

**Bottleneck.** A causal tile's K-loop trip count follows its query block index, so a balanced schedule pairs a long tile with a short one. CLC resolves the dispatch order in hardware, and at 1.73 tiles per CTA a coordinate remapping cannot steer it: the two tile durations of a CTA correlate at +0.21, against cuDNN's -0.81. **Change.** At no more than two tiles per CTA, use the static persistent scheduler: a CTA advances by `gridDim.x`, so its tiles are fixed. Rank them by descending trip count, traversed forwards on even rounds and backwards on odd ones. Applied unconditionally at 3.46 tiles per CTA this costs 7%, hence the guard. **Result.** The correlation moves to -0.76. `b8 h8 s1024` goes 778 → 864 TFLOP/s, past cuDNN's 821. ## Testing Measured at `b8 h8 s1024`, `b8 h16 s1024`, `b4 h32 s1024` and `b2 h16 s4096`, head_dim=128, fp16, causal, on B300 (148 SMs). Output is bitwise identical to `main` at every shape, with no NaN. Shapes that do not satisfy the static-pairing condition, and launches without `FA_CLC`, are unchanged.

title: [Sm90, fwd] refine UseSchedulerBarrier heuristic for kHeadDim=128
body:
## Background

In the Hopper (SM90) TMA-based mainloop, `UseSchedulerBarrier` is a heuristic used to control instruction scheduling and overlap between Warp Groups. Currently, for non-FP8 data types, this barrier is enabled for `kHeadDim <= 128`.

## Changes

This PR adjusts the threshold from `kHeadDim <= 128` to `kHeadDim < 128`. When `kHeadDim` is exactly 128, disabling the scheduler barrier reduces synchronization overhead between warp groups.
